session.question: How do innovation, CEOs' sustainability orientation, and green governance relate to sustainability and environmental performance in firms?
session.answer:
Innovation, CEOs’ sustainability orientation (SO), and green governance are all linked to improved sustainability and environmental performance, but they operate through different mechanisms. In firms where CEOs exhibit stronger sustainability orientation, environmental performance tends to improve directly, although this effect can be weakened by financial slack or political connections. This indicates that SO is a positive strategic driver, but its impact is contingent on firm-level resources and ties. (adomako2021chiefexecutiveofficers chunk 1)

Innovation is a central transmission mechanism. In Norwegian maritime firms, long-term orientation was not directly associated with emission reductions; instead, green strategy and green innovation mediated the relationship and were themselves directly associated with lower greenhouse-gas and other harmful emissions. Similarly, in Saudi Arabian SMEs, organizational environmental culture improved environmental sustainability and environmental performance through green HRM and green innovation. Thus, innovation-related practices translate sustainability orientation or culture into measurable environmental gains. (sæther2021sustainabilityamongnorwegian chunk 1, doghan2022organizationalenvironmentalculture chunk 1)

Green governance contributes by aligning managerial, board, and ownership structures with environmental innovation. In dirty firms, multiple governance configurations involving CEO power, board capital, and ownership structure were sufficient for high environmental innovation, showing that both strong and weak CEOs can support innovation when matched with appropriate governance bundles. Overall, green governance and innovation function as complementary mechanisms that enable sustainability orientation at the top of the firm to be converted into better sustainability and environmental performance outcomes. (shui2022sustainablecorporategovernance chunk 1, doghan2022organizationalenvironmentalculture chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-be035065: The excerpt describes a study on organizational environmental culture (OEC), environmental sustainability (ES), and environmental performance (EP) in Saudi Arabian SMEs. It finds that OEC positively and significantly affects green HRM and green innovation (GI), and that green HRM and GI are significant predictors of ES and EP. Importantly, green HRM and GI mediate the relationships between OEC and both ES and EP. The study used survey data from 236 respondents and SEM analysis. This suggests that governance-related practices and innovation serve as mechanisms connecting sustainability orientation at the top management level to improved sustainability and environmental performance.
From Mohammed A. Al Doghan, Nadia A. Abdelmegeed Abdelwahed, Bahadur Ali Soomro, and Mahmoud M. H. Alayis. Organizational environmental culture, environmental sustainability and performance: the mediating role of green hrm and green innovation. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14127510, doi:10.3390/su14127510.

pqac-e4587901: The excerpt discusses how environmental innovation in firms is shaped by corporate governance bundles involving CEOs, boards, and ownership. It finds six sufficient configurations for high environmental innovation among 250 dirty firms, showing multiple paths to achieving it. Both powerful and weak CEOs can facilitate environmental innovation when paired with suitable board capital and ownership structures. The study emphasizes the interdependence of CEO power (formal and informal), board capital (breadth and depth), and ownership (institutional and insider) in driving environmental innovation, which is closely related to sustainability and environmental performance.
From Xiaolong Shui, Minhao Zhang, Palie Smart, and Fei Ye. Sustainable corporate governance for environmental innovation: a configurational analysis on board capital, ceo power and ownership structure. Journal of Business Research, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbusres.2022.05.037, doi:10.1016/j.jbusres.2022.05.037.

pqac-744ac6e0: The excerpt studies Norwegian maritime firms and finds that long-term orientation is not directly associated with emission reductions, but it is indirectly related through green strategy and green innovation. Green strategy and green innovation act as mediators, each having direct associations with firms’ reductions of greenhouse gases and other environmentally harmful emissions. Although the paper does not specifically mention “green governance,” it suggests that strategic and innovation-related green practices translate a leader’s sustainability orientation into better environmental outcomes, including emission reduction. The study uses a structural equation model based on 246 survey responses.
From Erik Andreas Sæther, Ann Elida Eide, and Øyvind Bjørgum. Sustainability among norwegian maritime firms: green strategy and innovation as mediators of long‐term orientation and emission reduction. Business Strategy and the Environment, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/bse.2752, doi:10.1002/bse.2752.

pqac-25074b66: The excerpt describes a study on CEOs’ sustainability orientation (SO) and firm environmental performance (FEP). It reports that SO is positively related to FEP among 297 SMEs in Ghana. The study also examines firm-level contingencies, finding that the positive SO–FEP relationship becomes weaker or negative when firms have stronger financial slack or stronger political connections. No information is provided about innovation or green governance in this excerpt.
From Samuel Adomako, Joseph Amankwah‐Amoah, Albert Danso, and George Obeng Dankwah. Chief executive officers' sustainability orientation and firm environmental performance: networking and resource contingencies. Business Strategy and the Environment, 2021. contexts.context: This excerpt is about green innovation within firms, not directly about CEOs’ sustainability orientation or green governance. It finds that two internal factors matter for green innovation: green market orientation and absorptive capacity. In a survey of 262 Chinese manufacturing firms, green market orientation improves green product innovation but not process innovation, while green absorptive capacity improves both product and process innovation. Their interaction also positively affects both types of green innovation. The paper suggests that pursuing green market intelligence and technological knowledge supports green innovation outcomes, which may be relevant to sustainability performance, but it does not directly test CEOs or governance effects.
contexts.question: How do innovation, CEOs' sustainability orientation, and green governance relate to sustainability and environmental performance in firms?

contexts.context: The excerpt is about how institutional pressures, green innovation, entrepreneurial orientation, and sustainable performance are linked. It finds that regulatory, normative, and cognitive pressures positively affect green innovation, and entrepreneurial orientation mediates this relationship. Green innovation is associated with sustainable performance, but entrepreneurial orientation negatively moderates the green innovation–performance link when firms have insufficient green innovation, because higher risk-taking can undermine performance. The paper suggests institutional pressure can stimulate firms to adopt innovative environmental practices. It does not directly discuss CEOs’ sustainability orientation or green governance, but it is relevant to the broader theme of innovation and environmental/sustainability performance in firms.
contexts.question: How do innovation, CEOs' sustainability orientation, and green governance relate to sustainability and environmental performance in firms?

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How do innovation, CEOs' sustainability orientation, and green governance relate to sustainability and environmental performance in firms?

Innovation, CEOs’ sustainability orientation (SO), and green governance are all linked to improved sustainability and environmental performance, but they operate through different mechanisms. In firms where CEOs exhibit stronger sustainability orientation, environmental performance tends to improve directly, although this effect can be weakened by financial slack or political connections. This indicates that SO is a positive strategic driver, but its impact is contingent on firm-level resources and ties. (adomako2021chiefexecutiveofficers chunk 1)

Innovation is a central transmission mechanism. In Norwegian maritime firms, long-term orientation was not directly associated with emission reductions; instead, green strategy and green innovation mediated the relationship and were themselves directly associated with lower greenhouse-gas and other harmful emissions. Similarly, in Saudi Arabian SMEs, organizational environmental culture improved environmental sustainability and environmental performance through green HRM and green innovation. Thus, innovation-related practices translate sustainability orientation or culture into measurable environmental gains. (sæther2021sustainabilityamongnorwegian chunk 1, doghan2022organizationalenvironmentalculture chunk 1)

Green governance contributes by aligning managerial, board, and ownership structures with environmental innovation. In dirty firms, multiple governance configurations involving CEO power, board capital, and ownership structure were sufficient for high environmental innovation, showing that both strong and weak CEOs can support innovation when matched with appropriate governance bundles. Overall, green governance and innovation function as complementary mechanisms that enable sustainability orientation at the top of the firm to be converted into better sustainability and environmental performance outcomes. (shui2022sustainablecorporategovernance chunk 1, doghan2022organizationalenvironmentalculture chunk 1)
